messages:
sam: FYI — after the dedupe/merge window change we saw attribution jitter and an ~18% cost spike for model-inference routes.
anya: Ugh. Got the alert — devops-bot flagged trace-merge-rate. link: https://grafana.company/redwood/d/abc123/trace-merge?orgId=1
louis: Is this the late-join enrichment causing duplicate token counts? I can repro locally with a delayed kv cache hit.
sam: @louis prob. When span A is delayed and attaches to span B we end up double-counting tokens on the billing side.
nina: Quick check — did the new coalescer change the sample_key? that would break the dedupe heuristic.
louis: It did — coalescer now rewrites span.fingerprint -> span.hash_v2 and we didn't emit the old key.
anya: OK — immediate mitigation options: revert the rewrite, or emit both keys during a transition window.
sam: I prefer emitting both keys. Proposal runbook (short):
  1) Update coalescer to emit both keys (span.fingerprint + span.hash_v2).
  2) Deploy canary to 10% of traffic and monitor billing delta & duplicate-rate metric.
  3) After 24h, roll to 100% and keep dual-emit for 7 days.
  4) Backfill a mismatch metric and run a replay to audit historic double-counts.
nina: Also add a billing-side heuristic: treat events with same tenant/id and identical token_hash within merge_window_ms=3000 as duplicates to ignore.
louis: Example config snippet for canary:
```json
{"coalescer": {"emit_keys": ["span.fingerprint","span.hash_v2"], "merge_window_ms": 3000}}
```
anya: Add an automated eval: run the 12h replay job and assert cost delta < 2% vs baseline for the inference routes.
sam: Who can own the change + PR today? I'll draft the runbook doc in Confluence and list rollback steps.
louis: I'll open the PR now and tag @anya for review. ETA EOD.
devops-bot: alert cleared — trace-merge-rate back to baseline :white_check_mark:
sam: Thanks all. If we still see oddness we'll escalate in tomorrow's arch sync.
